q: The quantum complexity class QMA (Quantum Merlin-Arthur) is the quantum analogue of NP. The local Hamiltonian problem is QMA-complete, which means:
opts: Local Hamiltonians can be efficiently simulated
Determining whether the ground state energy is above or below a given threshold (with promise gap) is in QMA and every QMA problem reduces to it
All quantum algorithms are in QMA
Quantum computers can solve NP-complete problems efficiently
exp: The local Hamiltonian problem (Kitaev's theorem, 2002) is QMA-complete: it is in QMA and every QMA problem reduces to it. This is the quantum analogue of Cook-Levin (SAT is NP-complete) and launched quantum computational complexity theory.
